Neck pain is often linked to poor posture, prolonged screen time, muscle strain, or everyday stress. In many cases, simple lifestyle changes can help reduce discomfort naturally and improve neck mobility.

Start by maintaining good posture while sitting, standing, or using digital devices. Keep your screen at eye level and avoid looking down at your phone for long periods. Taking short movement breaks every 30–45 minutes helps prevent stiffness and reduces strain on the neck muscles.

Gentle stretching and strengthening exercises for the neck and upper back can improve flexibility and support the cervical spine. Sleeping with a supportive pillow, staying physically active, managing stress, and staying hydrated may also contribute to healthier muscles and joints.

While these measures help many people, persistent neck pain, pain spreading to the shoulder or arm, numbness, tingling, or weakness should be assessed to identify the underlying cause. Neck pain that keeps returning is often a sign that the underlying cause needs attention. Many people experience temporary relief with rest or medication, but the discomfort may come back if factors affecting the neck are not addressed.

Common reasons for recurring neck pain include poor posture, prolonged screen time, muscle weakness, stress-related tension, previous neck injuries, cervical disc problems, or age-related changes in the spine. Spending long hours looking down at mobile devices or working without proper ergonomic support can place continuous strain on the neck muscles and joints.

Some people may notice stiffness, restricted neck movement, shoulder pain, headaches, or pain spreading toward the arms. In certain cases, symptoms like tingling, numbness, or weakness may indicate nerve irritation and require proper evaluation.

Managing recurring neck pain involves more than temporary pain relief. Improving posture, strengthening neck and upper back muscles, maintaining healthy movement habits, and following appropriate exercises can support long-term spine health.

Patients near Charni Road often ask whether Pott’s spine can affect walking ability.

Pott’s spine is a type of spinal infection that can affect the bones, discs, and surrounding tissues of the spine. Many patients are concerned whether this condition can cause leg weakness or numbness, especially when symptoms progress over time.

In the early stages, Pott’s spine may cause persistent back pain, stiffness, fatigue, or discomfort. However, if the infection leads to swelling, bone damage, or pressure on the spinal cord or nerves, it can result in nerve-related symptoms such as tingling, numbness, leg weakness, difficulty walking, or changes in balance.

The severity of nerve symptoms depends on the location of infection, the amount of spinal cord or nerve compression, and how early treatment is started. Not every patient with Pott’s spine develops weakness or numbness, but these symptoms should not be ignored.

Diagnosis usually involves a detailed clinical assessment, blood tests, and imaging such as MRI to understand the extent of infection and nerve involvement. Early treatment with appropriate medical care helps control infection, protect nerve function, and reduce the risk of long-term complications.

Timely spine evaluation is important for patients experiencing persistent back pain with neurological symptoms. The goal is to preserve mobility, improve recovery, and support long-term spine health.

Patients near Charni Road often seek clarity about persistent pain around the lower back and pelvis.

The sacroiliac (SI) joint connects the spine to the pelvis and plays an important role in transferring weight and movement between the upper and lower body. When this joint becomes unstable, inflamed, or severely degenerated, it can cause persistent lower back pain, buttock pain, hip discomfort, or pain that worsens while standing, walking, or changing positions.

Most SI joint problems improve with non-surgical treatment such as physiotherapy, activity modification, medications, targeted injections, and strengthening exercises. However, surgery may be considered when symptoms continue for several months despite appropriate conservative care and significantly affect daily activities.

SI joint fusion surgery aims to stabilize the affected joint and reduce abnormal movement that may be contributing to pain. Not every patient with lower back pain requires SI joint fusion. The decision depends on symptom severity, response to previous treatments, overall health, and the impact on quality of life. Accurate diagnosis is essential, as SI joint pain can sometimes mimic other spine or hip conditions. Early assessment helps guide the most appropriate treatment plan and supports long-term mobility and function.

Careful assessment helps Charni Road patients make informed treatment choices.

Patients near Charni Road often ask whether spinal canal narrowing can affect leg strength.

Lumbar canal stenosis occurs when the spinal canal in the lower back becomes narrowed, placing pressure on the nerves that travel to the legs. Many patients worry that this condition may eventually lead to paralysis. In most cases, lumbar canal stenosis develops gradually and causes symptoms such as lower back pain, leg pain, numbness, tingling, heaviness in the legs, or difficulty walking long distances.

Complete paralysis from lumbar canal stenosis is uncommon. However, severe and untreated nerve compression can sometimes lead to significant weakness, loss of balance, reduced walking ability, or worsening nerve function. Certain warning signs require prompt medical attention, including progressive leg weakness, loss of bladder or bowel control, or numbness around the groin area.

The severity of symptoms does not always match the degree of narrowing seen on scans, which is why a detailed clinical assessment is important. Treatment may include activity modification, physiotherapy, posture correction, medication, or surgery in selected cases.

Early evaluation helps identify the extent of nerve compression and supports timely treatment decisions. The goal is to preserve mobility, protect nerve function, reduce symptoms, and maintain independence in daily life.

Early attention helps Charni Road patients maintain better mobility and nerve health.

Many people near Charni Road ask whether a slip disc can return after recovery.

A slip disc can improve with proper treatment, but in some cases, symptoms may return if the spine continues to experience excessive strain. Recurrence does not always mean the earlier treatment failed. The spine is constantly exposed to daily stress from sitting, lifting, bending, poor posture, obesity, weak core muscles, or physically demanding activities.

Many patients recover well with physiotherapy, medication, posture correction, and lifestyle changes. However, returning too quickly to heavy lifting, prolonged sitting, or improper exercise techniques may increase pressure on the spinal discs again. Smoking, lack of physical activity, and untreated spinal weakness can also affect long-term spine health.

Recurring symptoms may include lower back pain, leg pain, numbness, tingling, or stiffness similar to earlier episodes. In some cases, the symptoms are mild and temporary, while others may require further medical evaluation.

The focus after slip disc treatment is not only pain relief, but also preventing recurrence through spinal strengthening, posture awareness, ergonomic habits, and guided rehabilitation. Regular exercise, healthy body weight, and proper lifting techniques play an important role in protecting the spine over time.

Consistent spine care helps Charni Road patients protect long-term mobility.

Patients near Charni Road often seek expert guidance for complex spine conditions.

Spine reconstruction surgery is carefully planned based on the patient’s spinal condition, symptoms, posture balance, nerve pressure, and overall health. Spine surgeons do not follow a single approach for every patient. Instead, they study imaging scans, spinal alignment, movement patterns, bone quality, and the severity of deformity or instability before deciding the reconstruction strategy.

Conditions such as scoliosis, kyphosis, spinal instability, fractures, infection, or severe disc degeneration may require different surgical planning. The main goal is to restore spinal stability, protect nerves, improve alignment, and reduce pain while helping the patient maintain safe movement and daily function.

Surgeons also consider age, activity level, medical history, muscle strength, and recovery expectations before choosing the most suitable procedure. In some cases, minimally invasive techniques may be possible, while complex deformities may require staged reconstruction surgery.

Every spine behaves differently, which is why individualized planning is important. Careful preoperative evaluation helps reduce surgical risk and improves long-term outcomes. Modern spine reconstruction focuses not only on correcting structure, but also on supporting balance, mobility, and quality of life after recovery.

Structured evaluation helps Charni Road patients make informed treatment decisions.

Long working hours near Charni Road often contribute to posture-related spine stress.

Poor posture may seem harmless at first, but over time it can place continuous stress on the spine, muscles, and joints. Sitting for long hours with rounded shoulders, looking down at mobile phones, or standing unevenly can gradually affect spinal alignment and movement patterns.

In the early stages, posture-related changes are usually flexible and improve with exercise, stretching, and posture correction. However, when poor posture continues for years, the spine and surrounding soft tissues may adapt to that position. This can contribute to exaggerated spinal curves such as kyphosis or lordosis, muscle imbalance, stiffness, and ongoing neck or back pain.

People often notice symptoms like shoulder tightness, forward head posture, fatigue while sitting, or discomfort after long working hours. In some cases, poor posture may also increase pressure on spinal discs and joints, especially when combined with weak core muscles or a sedentary lifestyle.

The good news is that early attention can make a significant difference. Ergonomic adjustments, regular movement, posture training, strengthening exercises, and guided physiotherapy can help improve spinal balance and reduce strain. A clinical spine evaluation may help identify whether posture is causing temporary stress or more lasting structural changes.

Healthy posture habits help Charni Road residents reduce daily spinal strain.

Patients near Charni Road often ask whether tingling after surgery is part of normal healing.

After spine surgery, many patients expect nerve pain, numbness, or weakness to disappear immediately. However, nerves usually heal gradually over time. When a nerve has been compressed by a slipped disc, spinal stenosis, or long-standing pressure, it often needs time to recover even after the pressure is removed.

During the healing process, some patients may continue to feel tingling, burning sensations, mild numbness, or intermittent leg or arm pain. This does not always mean the surgery has failed. In many cases, it reflects the natural recovery process of irritated nerves. The speed of healing depends on factors such as the duration of nerve compression, overall health, diabetes, smoking, and the severity of the original condition.

Gentle movement, guided physiotherapy, proper posture, hydration, and adequate sleep all support nerve recovery after spine surgery. Avoiding heavy lifting and following rehabilitation advice are equally important for long-term healing.

Regular follow-up helps monitor recovery and identify whether symptoms are improving as expected. Patience is important, as nerves often heal more slowly than muscles or bones. The focus after surgery is not only pain relief, but also restoring safe movement, stability, and daily function.

Proper spine rehabilitation helps Charni Road patients recover safely.

Long travel hours near Charni Road can trigger sciatica pain.

Traveling with sciatica can be uncomfortable, but the right precautions can help you stay mobile and reduce nerve irritation. Sciatica pain usually travels from the lower back to the leg, and long periods of sitting during travel can increase pressure on the spine.

One of the most important tips is to avoid sitting for too long. During long journeys, try to stand, stretch, or walk every 30–45 minutes whenever possible. Using a small lumbar support or rolled towel behind the lower back helps maintain the natural spinal curve and reduces strain.

Choose a comfortable seat with proper back support, and keep your hips and knees at a relaxed angle. Avoid keeping your wallet or bulky items in your back pocket, as this can increase nerve pressure. Staying hydrated and doing gentle ankle and leg movements can also improve circulation.

If pain is active, avoid lifting heavy luggage or sudden twisting movements. A pre-travel spine check with a specialist can help ensure your condition is stable. With simple planning, most people with sciatica can travel safely and comfortably.

⚖️ MYTH vs FACT

❌ Myth: Every Slip Disc Requires Surgery

✅ Fact: Most patients improve without surgery.

A slip disc diagnosis can be worrying, but surgery is not the answer for everyone. In fact, most patients recover successfully with medications, physiotherapy, lifestyle modifications, and guided rehabilitation.

Surgery is generally reserved for selected situations such as persistent severe pain, progressive neurological weakness, or loss of bladder and bowel control.

The most important principle in spine care is to treat the patient's symptoms and clinical condition—not just the MRI report.

If you are experiencing back pain, leg pain, or have concerns about your MRI findings, a proper clinical evaluation can help determine the best treatment approach.

🦴 *SPINE TIP OF THE WEEK*

*THE 10-SECOND SCOLIOSIS CHECK*
*Could Your Child Have a Curved Spine?*

Many children with scoliosis have *no pain at all*, which is why it often goes unnoticed until the curve becomes more obvious.

The good news? A simple 10-second check at home can help identify early warning signs.

👀 *What to look for:*
✅ One shoulder higher than the other
✅ Uneven waistline
✅ One side of the rib cage appearing more prominent
✅ Leaning to one side while standing
✅ Uneven posture in photographs

💡 *Try this simple test:*
Ask your child to stand with feet together, bend forward, and touch their toes while you observe from behind.

Early detection can make a significant difference, especially during growth spurts between *10–16 years of age*.

Remember:
👉 Not every uneven shoulder means scoliosis.
👉 But if you notice any of these signs, it's worth getting the spine evaluated.

A quick 10-second check today could make a lifelong difference tomorrow.

📤 Please share this with parents, teachers, coaches, school groups, and anyone involved in children's health and development. Early awareness matters. 😊

🏃‍♂️ Spine Tip of the Week | The Runner's Paradox

Many runners have excellent cardiovascular fitness and endurance, but running alone may not fully protect against age-related muscle loss (sarcopenia), reduced strength, or declining bone health.

While running trains your heart, strength training helps protect your muscles, bones, joints, and spine.

Benefits of regular strength training for runners:
✅ Improved running efficiency
✅ Better spine support
✅ Reduced injury risk
✅ Stronger muscles and bones
✅ Prevention of age-related muscle loss

A simple goal: For every 3–4 running sessions per week, include at least 2 strength-training sessions. Even 20 minutes twice weekly can make a meaningful difference.

At Bombay Spine Clinic, we encourage runners and active individuals to focus on both endurance and strength for long-term spine health and injury prevention.

Dr. Siddharth Katkade | Consultant Spine Surgeon

🦴 Spine Tip of the Week | Text Neck Syndrome

Do you spend several hours daily looking at your phone, laptop, or tablet?

Prolonged screen use can place excessive stress on the cervical spine, leading to a condition commonly known as **Text Neck Syndrome**. As the head tilts forward, the load on the neck muscles and cervical discs increases significantly, contributing to neck pain, shoulder stiffness, headaches, poor posture, and upper back discomfort.

A simple habit can help:
✅ Hold your phone closer to eye level
✅ Avoid prolonged neck flexion
✅ Take movement breaks every 20–30 minutes
✅ Perform gentle neck and upper back stretches regularly

At Bombay Spine Clinic, we frequently see patients with posture-related neck pain, cervical spondylosis, office-related neck strain, and screen-time-associated spine problems.

Early attention to posture and ergonomics can help reduce long-term stress on the spine and improve overall neck health.

🦴 Spine Tip of the Week | Healthy Hips, Strong Spine

Did you know tight hips and pelvic imbalance can contribute to lower back pain, poor posture, stiffness, and reduced spinal mobility?

Limited hip mobility forces the lower back to compensate, increasing stress on the lumbar spine over time. Simple hip mobility exercises and pelvic tilt movements can help improve posture, reduce back strain, and support a healthier spine.

Prolonged screen time and desk work can contribute to neck pain, upper back stiffness, eye strain, poor posture, and “tech neck syndrome.”

A simple evidence-based habit that helps:
✅ Every 20 minutes
✅ Look 20 feet away
✅ For 20 seconds

The 20-20-20 rule helps relax neck muscles, reduce screen fatigue, improve posture, and decrease strain on the cervical spine. Simple neck stretches during work breaks can further support spinal health and mobility.

Degenerative Cervical Myelopathy (DCM) is often missed in routine OPD practice and treated as simple cervical spondylosis.

Early clues include:
✔️ Hand clumsiness
✔️ Gait imbalance or frequent falls
✔️ Hoffmann’s positive sign
✔️ Progressive weakness or stiffness
✔️ Bilateral upper limb symptoms

🚨 Red Flags Requiring Urgent Referral:
* Bowel/bladder dysfunction
* Rapidly progressive weakness
* Severe gait instability

📌 MRI Cervical Spine remains the gold standard investigation.

Early diagnosis and timely referral can prevent irreversible neurological decline and improve patient outcomes.

featured_reviews.review_text:
If you have ever watched your parent live with constant knee pain, trying one medicine after another, hoping and praying for relief but never truly getting better, you will understand exactly how I feel today.

For 10–12 years, my mother suffered from advanced arthritis. She was homebound, struggled to walk, couldn’t climb stairs, and slowly began losing hope that she would ever regain a normal, pain-free life. Surgery had been suggested years ago, but she was never fully confident. So she kept postponing it, hoping something else would work.

Then we met Dr. Sachin Rathod.

From our very first consultation, we felt we were in the right place. He was warm, patient, and incredibly easy to talk to. We did not feel rushed. He answered every question calmly, explained the entire process clearly, and most importantly, gave us realistic expectations. He didn’t push us, he gave us clarity and confidence to decide.

In today’s world, where many doctors seem rushed or inaccessible, Dr. Rathod is truly different. If you want someone who listens—really listens - he is that doctor. You can openly discuss health concerns, risks, costs, pre-operative and post-operative doubts - anything. He responds personally. Not through assistants. Not after days of waiting. Often within minutes or a few hours, and it is always him. That level of accessibility and dedication is rare.

One incident truly touched us. He had promised to visit my mother one day but was held up due to other commitments. We assumed he might not make it. Yet, late that night, he came—just as promised. He didn’t rush. He spent time with her, examined her carefully, reassured her, and patiently answered our concerns. That moment showed us that his commitment goes far beyond routine duty.

Initially, we thought we would take a second opinion and wait another month or two. But after meeting him, we were certain. Within two weeks of completing the required tests (which he had already guided us about during our first visit), my mother underwent bilateral total knee replacement surgery.

The surgery lasted five hours.
When she came out, something had changed; not just physically, but mentally. She was positive and motivated. Dr. Rathod was not just a surgeon; he was a counselor, guide, and motivator.

His care did not end after surgery. He personally made her walk on the first day. On the second day, she even climbed a couple of steps. For all four days in the hospital, he remained present and involved. He never disappeared after the procedure or delegated everything to assistants.

Even during recovery, he stayed accessible. We could send reports on WhatsApp, clarify doubts anytime, and receive guidance promptly. In this busy digital age, having a doctor who is reachable, responsive, and completely ego-free is remarkable.

Within just 6-7 days, my mother was able to bend her knees up to 85–90 degrees. Even the physiotherapist mentioned that this reflected excellent surgical technique and precision.

But beyond the medical success, what moves me most is this: for as long as I remember, my mother’s legs were bent due to arthritis. Today, they are straight. She is walking again with strength, confidence, and hope. It truly feels like she has been given a new set of knees and a renewed mindset.

If you are watching your parent suffer from severe knee pain, please do not hesitate to consult Dr. Sachin Rathod. He will listen. He will guide you honestly. And he will stand by you, not just during surgery, but beyond it.

He is not just an exceptional orthopedic surgeon, he is a compassionate human being.

We are deeply grateful.
